process: Human directive (this session): generate all 8 remaining enemies x 2 variants in one pass, no gate between them; human picks winners; then one animation loop per winner. Band-by-hue is dead. Body colour varies per enemy for visual variety.
rules_applied: Band gradient killed: colour no longer encodes contact damage. Size already does it, and the four free giants break any body-level band claim (Giant Howlback deals 19 on a band-B body; Giant Snare Bloom deals 29, off the scale).
Body material colour is the variety axis, read off each kind's existing drawn colour in ENEMIES (config.ts). Wave 2 proved material colour on a body is the strongest separator in a 300-alive crowd.
Grafts go on the HEAD or shoulders, never the chest (wave 2: 0 for 4 on chest).
No 'remove anatomy', no 'the <object> is the torso' (documented failure modes, #218).
Emissive hue only on eyes or a large flat surface; hardware takes a material colour, not a glow (#219, #220).
Generation size = max(width, height) of the kind's MAD_FOREST_FRAMES entry, because spriteEnemyScale draws every sprite at one world scale.

enemies.label: Snare Bloom
enemies.prompt: big-headed short-armed humanoid figure made of wet dark bog-green rotted wood, a huge flower head with a wide open jaw lined with pale bone teeth and a ring of drooping dark petals around it, glowing acid green light down its open throat, dark green body, black outline
enemies.separates_from: Mute Bloom (26px, navy body, magenta cross) by 2x size, green body and open jaws
enemies.finding: A landed the brief outright: petal-hooded head, wide jaw, acid-green lit teeth and throat, bog-green body. The non-humanoid graft works on the head, as wave 1 found.

animation_plan.action: slow heavy lumbering walk on short legs, huge flower head swaying side to side, jaws held open
animation_plan.why: 80 speed, 500 HP, the largest body in the game. Shares its speed with The Shear, so cadence separates them by build (#220). Jaws stay OPEN across the loop: the acid-green throat is its only accent and #220 found the generator animates a lit mark away if given the chance.

winner.name: Snare Bloom A
winner.action: slow heavy lumbering walk on short legs, huge flower head swaying side to side, jaws held open
winner.why: 80 speed, 500 HP, the largest body in the game. Shares its speed with The Shear, so cadence separates them by build (#220). Jaws stay OPEN across the loop: the acid-green throat is its only accent and #220 found the generator animates a lit mark away if given the chance.

enemies.label: The Shear
enemies.prompt: broad-shouldered humanoid figure with very long arms made of wet dark rotted wood, a long lighting-truss blade of dark gunmetal scaffolding grafted onto each forearm, glowing violet light along the blade edges, dark purple-grey body, black outline
enemies.finding: A came back with NO blades at all - a plain purple-grey humanoid. B landed small violet blade tips on both forearms plus magenta eyes. Arms are a weak graft site (~50%); the head remains the only reliable one. The arms_length 2.0 proportion landed on both.

animation_plan.action: slow deliberate walk, very long bladed arms swinging wide
animation_plan.why: same 80 speed as Snare Bloom; a step quicker because the long arms carry the motion.

winner.name: The Shear B
winner.action: slow deliberate walk, very long bladed arms swinging wide
winner.why: same 80 speed as Snare Bloom; a step quicker because the long arms carry the motion.

enemies.label: Woofer

animation_plan.action: heavy wide walk, broad shoulders rocking, arms hanging
animation_plan.why: 140 speed but knockback 0.1 - it wades through a build rather than being pushed. Heavy cadence on a fast mover.

winner.name: Woofer A
winner.action: heavy wide walk, broad shoulders rocking, arms hanging
winner.why: 140 speed but knockback 0.1 - it wades through a build rather than being pushed. Heavy cadence on a fast mover.

service_findings: 8 of 24 create_character calls failed with 'Generation failed due to heavy load'; none were charged. 16 completed = 16 generations spent.
Failures cluster when more than ~4 jobs are in flight. Two to three concurrent is safe; six produced four failures in a row.
Refines #219's stall rule: a job pinned at a NON-95% percentage with a maxed ETA is also dead. Howlback B sat at 19%/~900s for 25 minutes while jobs fired after it completed, then had to be re-fired.
A dropped MCP transport can lose the call entirely - Echo Shard B never appeared in list_characters, so retrying was correct.

animation_fixed.warning: template mode animates ALL directions by default (1 gen each = 8 generations). If Howlback falls back to template, directions:['south'] is mandatory.
animation_fixed.fallback_rule: #220: switch to mode template after two v3 stalls on the same character.
